Subject: Compliance platform renewal — evidence mapping & concurrency credits

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're starting budget reviews for H2 and need to lock the compliance platform choice and scope. Two outstanding items from our side:

1) Evidence ownership for audit windows — who will be responsible for collecting and retaining screenshots, logs, and API evidence during SOC-like reviews? We need a clear handoff so our legal team signs off.

2) Concurrency credits — during our peak release windows we run a lot of short-lived infra changes. Can we get a temporary boost in concurrent scan/agent credits for onboarding or get a time-windowed credit applied in year 1?

I attached a lightly filled evidence mapping (evidence_mapping.xlsx) to show our current tooling and where we expect the platform to pull data. Also copied our procurement timeline: PO required by 07/09 to meet our Q3 rollout.

Action items: can Redwood confirm proposed evidence ownership model and whether you can include a 3-month onboarding concurrency credit in pricing?

Thanks,
Emily

Head of IT Compliance
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Compliance platform renewal — evidence mapping & concurrency credits

Emily,

Appreciate the clear summary and the map — very helpful. Quick answers and next steps below.

Evidence ownership: by default Redwood stores collected evidence in the customer's private workspace and retains the artifacts per the customer's retention policy. For audits, we provide an export bundle (audit package) and live access to the evidence portal. We propose the following responsibilities:
- Acme provides the initial connectors and mapping (we can help map common sources)
- Redwood manages scheduled collection, normalization, and time-stamped artifacts in the private workspace
- During formal audits, Acme grants read access to the auditor or requests a packaged export

This model keeps ownership with Acme while letting Redwood guarantee collection integrity. If Legal needs a stronger attestation, we can add a clause in the SOW about retention guarantees and signed export hashes.

Concurrency credits: we can offer a temporary onboarding credit for elevated concurrency (up to 3x baseline) for up to 90 days. Two options:
A) Time-bound credit included in year-1 pricing (no additional PO)
B) Discounted add-on that you can activate for a max of 90 days

I'll draft both options in the pricing PDF and SOW (proposed_pricing_v2.pdf and SOW_onboarding_draft.docx).

Next steps: Marissa — can you take point on the formal SOW wording for the attestation and credits? Sean — can you confirm any infra/agent install concerns from the ops side? Emily — if the PO timeline of 07/09 is fixed, we should aim to finalize terms by 07/02 so procurement can route.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks — looping in Rishi (security) to confirm attestation language. Rishi, high level ask from Acme: they want a clause that states Redwood will provide tamper-evident audit exports and a contact for evidence production requests within 48 hours. Is that acceptable from our controls & legal perspective?

Emily — I did a quick pass on the attached evidence_mapping and flagged three high-risk integrations (internal ticketing, CI logs, and EHR export). Can you confirm which of those you expect the vendor to pull automatically vs. provide a pushed feed? That will impact the effort estimate and whether the onboarding credit is sufficient.

Also noting procurement comment: Acme prefers a single-year contract with an optional auto-renew for year 2 — they want the onboarding uplift priced into year 1 rather than as a separate billed item. We should capture both pricing options in the PDF.

Hi all,

Quick chime in from the vendor perspective (Vanta). Appreciate the details — two notes that might help Acme weigh options:

1) Evidence ownership: our standard is similar to what Avery outlined. We store evidence in the customer's workspace and provide cryptographic export options. If Acme needs an explicit attestation, we can include an Appendix in the order that commits to 48-hour evidence production for audit requests (subject to scope).

2) Concurrency/onboarding credits: we can do a 60-day full concurrency uplift to 3x or a 90-day uplift to 2x, whichever fits your risk profile. If trying to avoid a price bump in year 1, option 2 (90-day 2x included) tends to be more budget-friendly.

If helpful, I can prepare a short comparison matrix showing how Vanta and Trust Center handle these two items; Marco from Trust Center copied here can do the same.
